native_result.query: The effect of which variable on BA degree completion decreases from 0.3636 to -0.2293 (while becoming insignifcant) when both race and academic characteristics are included in analysis?
native_result.HypoA: The effect of SES on BA degree completion decreases from 0.3636  (significant) to  -0.2293 (insignificant) and effect of race on BA degree completion decreases from 0.5024  (significant) to 0.0923 (insignificant) when academic characteristics are considered.
native_result.HypoB: Socioeconomic status (SES) is the variable whose effect on BA degree completion reverses. In a bivariate logit, higher SES predicts degree completion (coefficient ≈ +0.36 on a unit-variance scale, ≈ +0.47 raw, p<.001). Once race and academic characteristics (ability test composite and class percentile) are added, the SES coefficient flips to ≈ −0.23 and its significance is lost — a suppression pattern indicating SES mainly captures race/ability-related advantage that is directly modeled by the controls, leaving only a small negative residual association.
